sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellants submits that tribunal has committed error in holding the income of the deceased Rs.15,000/- per year.
She further submits that deceased was skilled driver and was earning Rs.5,000/- per month with Rs.70/- per day allowance.
So claims tribunal has committed error in holding income of the deceased Rs.15000/- per year.
Claims tribunal has committed error in awarding amount in the head of consortium and other heads so prays that just and proper amount of compensation may be awarded.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/insurance company supported of the findings recorded by the claims tribunal and prayed for rejection of the appeal and also argued that this appeal was dismissed for want of prosecution on 25.04.2018 and it was restored on 14.08.2023 and thereafter it was again dismissed on 16.02.2024 and then it was restored on 08.05.2024 so appellant is not entitled to get interest for this period.

6. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and perusal of the record of the case, it is found that claimants have not adduced driving licence of the deceased so without proving driving licence of the deceased, it cannot be presumed that deceased was a driver.
So claims tribunal has rightly held that at the time of the accident, the deceased was not second driver of the vehicle.

7. After perusal of the record, it is found that the accident occurred on 12.06.2009 and tribunal assessed the income of the deceased Rs.15,000/-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:24041 --3- per year which is not just and proper.
Income of the deceased must be assessed as per Minimum Wages Act and according to Minimum Wages Act, at that that time the income of unskilled person was Rs.3070/- per month.
So in the considered opinion of this Court, income of the deceased must be assessed as Rs.3070/- per month.

8. After perusal of the record, it is found that claims tribunal has committed error in not granting future prospects according to National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & others- 2017 ACJ 2700.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At the time of the accident, deceased was aged 40 years so 40% of the income must be added for future prospects.
Perusal of the record, it is found that there are 6 persons were dependent upon him so 1/4 th income must be deducted towards personal expenses.
9. In view of the aforesaid discussion, the compensation amount deserves to be enhanced.

Hence,
the break-up of enhancement in the compensation amount is as under:-
 Heads Calcu  Future prospects Income taken Rs.30 prospects)= Rs.4298/- p.m. X 12= Rs.51,576/- per annum X 15 (multiplier)=7,73,640/-

After deducting 1/4th amount (Rs.1,93,410/-) towards personal expenses, the amount comes to Rs.5,80,230/-

NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:24041 --4- 10.
Keeping in view the aforesaid, present appeal is allowed in part to the extent indicated herein above.
The amount of compensation is enhanced from Rs.1,47,000/- to Rs.8,77,230/- with interest as fixed by the tribunal over and above the amount already awarded by the tribunal.
Hence, the total amount enhanced in this appeal is Rs.7,30,230/- (Rs.8,77,230 -1,47,000/-).
Accordingly, the appellants shall be entitled to receive the enhanced amount of Rs.7,30,230/- over and and above the amount which has already been awarded by the tribunal.
All other findings recorded by the tribunal shall remain intact.
It is made clear that the claimants/appellants shall not be entitled to get interest for the period in which appeal was not in existence.
The present appeal stands disposed of.
